newsitem.title: USA: RJR says FTC asks for no new Joe Camel data.
newsitem.headline: RJR says FTC asks for no new Joe Camel data.

text.p: R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co said on Wednesday that the U.S. Federal Trade Commission has not asked any new questions about the company's Joe Camel advertising campaign.

The Wall Street Journal reported today that U.S. Federal Trade Commission staff members are asking the agency to bring an unfair advertising case against the tobacco company for aiming its advertising at youths.
R.J. Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, said there has been no substantive research since June 1994 that would change an earlier FTC study on the matter.
RJR said the FTC found in 1994 that there was no basis for the company to file a complaint against the Joe Camel campaign.

RJR said 95 percent of youths aged 10 through 17 recognized Joe Camel as a logo for cigarettes in a 1994 study. Of the 1,100 youths surveyed, 97 percent had extremely negative views about cigarettes, it said.
